name: sales-pre-call-brief
expected_output: Backlog choice, then the five-part interview in order with the recipe in Part 3, a method follow-up for the step after the student stops, today-versus-ideal follow-up with a plain-words playback of the long answer, fixed and gate questions, the four Part 5 draft messages, Value & Measurement close, the labels preview, and a saved single requirements file.
preconditions: When the AI asked whether that is how the student does it today, the student gave the script's long paragraph in one reply
When the AI asked what comes after the student's first method answer, the student said "then I read it and add my own questions"
When the AI asked the send-back question, the student also volunteered that the brief must never name another client
When the AI asked whether the LinkedIn notes-doc step should stay, the student said no

expectations.text: The first message contains the opening said exactly as in the spec (section 2), beginning "Deconstruct turns this workflow into a clear, testable description of what it must do.", followed by the switch line "I'll explain the questions that need it, and 'not sure' is always a fine answer. If you've done this before, say 'skip the explanations'."

checks.text: Deconstruct turns this workflow into a clear, testable description of what it must do. You'll finish with your Workflow Requirements, saved to

It's the most thorough conversation in the framework, about 25–40 minutes (longer for regulated work), because everything built later comes from what we capture here. It runs in five parts: (1) what this is worth, (2) scope and a name, (3) the outcome, (4) the path, and (5) rules, where you check or approve its work, the sources it uses, and how you'll judge it. Design reads it next to decide how the workflow gets built.
Stopping early is safe: progress is saved, and 'continue my workflow' picks up where we left off.
I'll explain the questions that need it, and 'not sure' is always a fine answer. If you've done this before, say 'skip the explanations'.

expectations.text: Each part opens with "Part N of 5", Part 1 to Part 5 in order
No part announces its own time (no minutes on a "Part N of 5" line)
Every AI message asks at most one question (a draft message ending "What's wrong or missing?" counts as one)
The label "Ask:" never appears in any AI message
The words step-driven and goal-driven never appear in any AI message
The AI never asks the student to choose a path type (steps versus goal)

`requirements.md` has the 12 sections of spec section 4a in this order and no others: `# [Name] — Workflow Requirements`, `## Goal`, `## Value & Measurement`, `## Metadata`, `## Path`, `## Inputs`, `## Context Inventory`, `## Acceptance Criteria`, `## Example Scenarios`, `## Rules & Constraints`, `## Human Gates`, `## Security, Privacy & Safety` (so no `## Sequence` and no `## Optimization Notes`)
`requirements.md` has no YAML frontmatter
`requirements.md` has no `Definition Type` row and no Sequence or Optimization Notes heading at any level
`## Human Gates` opens with the line `Runs: with you` or `Runs: without you`
`## Security, Privacy & Safety` contains the line `Governing regime: …` before a `### Writes` heading; under `### Writes` there is either a `- W1 · …` line or the line `None`

Every line under `## Path` that is a step is written `- Step N — [Name] · produces …` with a `fixed (…)` or `flexible` mark, optional tags in the spec's order (uses, fixed/flexible, writes, role, parallel with, proposed by AI)
`framework/[name]/deconstruct-in-progress.md` existed during the interview and is deleted once `requirements.md` is written
The AI says nothing about the progress file (its name never appears in an AI message)

The close is said word for word: "Workflow Requirements saved to `framework/[name]/requirements.md`. It holds your goal, [N] steps, [M] context items, [K] acceptance criteria, and [J] test inputs. Step 3, Design, reads this file and decides how the workflow gets built — as a skill or an agent, on your platform — in about 30 minutes. Start it with 'run the design skill' (in Claude Code, you can also type `/design` and pick it from the list)."
